title: FALSE > "true" is an error: a Boolean is not compared with text
query: EVALUATE ROW ( "r", IF ( FALSE () > "true", "Expression is true", "Expression is false" ) )

expected.error: comparison operations do not support comparing values of type True/False with values of type Text

source.quote: Other mixed data-type comparisons will return an error
source.supports: Boolean with String is not a supported pair

source.quote: =IF(FALSE()>"true","Expression is true", "Expression is false") returns "Expression is true"

derivation: The left operand is a Boolean and the right is text. That pair is not among the supported comparisons (Numeric with Numeric, Boolean with Boolean, String with String), so the query fails.
alternative: The Power BI data types page says this very formula returns "Expression is true" (a Boolean ranks above text): one row, [r] = "Expression is true" (string).
notes: The Microsoft pages disagree. The operator reference says a comparison of text (or a Boolean) with a number is an error. The Power BI data types page gives a result, ranking Boolean above text and text above numbers.
